guide.text: The sources are November 5, 2026 meeting notes and the FY2026 annual report from Ridgeline Return Works, a reentry jobs program in Carver Falls.
In FY2026, enrollment rose from 88 to 121 people, and permanent job placements rose from 47 to 69.
Six-month retention was 71 percent, but only 52 of 69 placements had reached six months, and the program had no comparison group.

chips.locator: “The result we are proudest of, and its limits”

guide.text: A second crew and a retention coach will add $186,000, which brings the FY2027 budget to $798,400.
The team agreed to ask the Pellwood Foundation for $90,000 and to raise the other $96,000 from current funders.

asks.what: A short deck for Pellwood's workforce reentry round asking for $90,000

brief.goal: Decide whether to fund $90,000 toward the $186,000 expansion

questions.text: Retention was 71 percent, short of the 75 percent target. The expansion adds $186,000, taking the budget from $612,400 to $798,400. Will that cost close a 4-point gap?

Slide 1: Ridgeline Return Works
Paid work from the first week home
Request to the Pellwood Foundation, Workforce Reentry Round
Carver Falls | December 2026

Slide 2: Two Years of Growth
People enrolled: 88 → 121 (+38%)
Placed in permanent jobs: 47 → 69 (+47%)
Average starting wage: $17.10 → $18.25
Employers hiring our people: 15 → 23
FY2025 to FY2026

Slide 3: How It Works
Paid crew work within 5 business days of intake, at $16.50/hour
Landscaping, light demolition and park cleanup contracts
A job coach helps with ID, resume, driver's license and interviews
Goal: a permanent job within 12 weeks
Support continues for 6 months after placement

Slide 4: Six-Month Job Retention
71% still employed six months after placement (FY2025: 58%)
Based on the 52 of 69 FY2026 placements that have reached six months
The 6 people we lost contact with are counted as not employed
We have no comparison group and do not claim the program caused the improvement
County unemployment also fell, from 5.1% to 4.4%

Slide 5: In His Words
"The crew paid me the first week. That's the part nobody else did. I didn't have to choose between rent and showing up."
Darnell, crew graduate, now on the night shift at Brannock Precast

Slide 6: What FY2026 Taught Us
The first 60 days on the job are when people lose work
People who stayed employed were far more likely to have had 3+ coach check-ins in those 60 days
Follow-up slipped because coaches were stretched across every phase
With one crew of 12, people waited up to 3 weeks to start
Four employers asked for more referrals than we could send

Slide 7: The FY2027 Expansion: $186,000
Second crew lead and crew supervisor stipend: $72,000
Dedicated retention coach: $64,000
Second crew vehicle lease and equipment: $28,000
Added participant supports: $22,000
Targets: 160 enrolled, 90 placed, 75% six-month retention
Retention measured the same way, with lost contacts counted as not employed

Slide 8: Our Request: $90,000
$90,000 from Pellwood: about half of the $186,000 expansion
The other $96,000 is being raised from current funders
The rest of the FY2027 budget, $612,400, is covered by existing sources
Total FY2027 budget: $798,400

Slide 9: Proven, Careful Stewardship
FY2026 cost per permanent placement: about $8,875
Revenue from county, two foundations, a community trust, 312 individual gifts and earned crew contracts
FY2026 closed with a small operating surplus
Marisol Okafor-Reyes, Executive Director
Ridgeline Return Works, Lowell Street, Carver Falls

P2.text:
Ridgeline Return Works
Staff and board development committee meeting notes
Thursday, November 5, 2026, 4:00 p.m., Lowell Street office

P3.text: Present: Marisol Okafor-Reyes (Executive Director), Glen Ashworth (Board Treasurer), Priya Venkataraman (Development Committee Chair), Tomas Beltran (Program Director)

P5.text: Priya reported that Anneke Lisle, program officer at the Pellwood Foundation, invited us to submit a short deck for their workforce reentry round after her October site visit. Pellwood does not take full proposals at this stage; they review decks first.

P6.text: Decision: ask Pellwood for $90,000 toward the $186,000 FY2027 expansion (second crew plus retention coach). Glen confirmed the rest of the FY2027 budget, $612,400, is covered by existing sources, so the deck should present $90,000 as about half of the expansion gap, with the other $96,000 being raised from current funders.

P7.text: Deadline: the deck goes to Anneke by Friday, December 4, 2026. Marisol wants a draft for review by November 24.

P8.text: 2. Instructions for the deck (agreed by all four)

P9.text:
- Keep it to ten slides or fewer. Anneke said Pellwood's committee reads decks on their phones.
- Lead with the two-year trend: 88 to 121 enrolled, 47 to 69 placed.
- Show the 71 percent six-month retention figure only with the caveat beside it: 52 of 69 placements have reached six months, and the 6 lost contacts are counted as not employed. Tomas was firm that we must not claim the program caused the improvement.
- Use Darnell's quote with first name only. Do not use any participant photos.
- Do not mention the county contract renewal as uncertain; Glen says it is not.

P11.text: Tomas pulls the final FY2026 numbers. Priya drafts. Glen checks every figure against the annual report before it goes out.

P13.text:
## FY2026 Annual Program Report
Fiscal year July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026
Carver Falls

P14.text:
Ridgeline Return Works helps people coming home from prison and county jail get into paid work and keep it. We run out of a converted tire shop on Lowell Street in Carver Falls, with six full-time staff, two part-time crew leads and a board of nine. Most of the people we serve were released to supervision in Tamsen County and have less than ninety days of freedom behind them when they walk through our door.
The model is simple and deliberately short on waiting. A participant starts on a paid transitional work crew within five business days of intake, earning $16.50 an hour on landscaping, light demolition and park cleanup contracts. While they work, a job coach helps them get identification, a resume, a driver's license where possible and interviews with local employers. The goal is a permanent job within twelve weeks, and support for the six months after that.

P15.text:
FY2026 was the year the waiting list caught up with us. Referrals from Tamsen County Probation and two state facilities rose sharply after the county added a reentry liaison position in the fall, and we expanded the crew schedule from four days a week to five to absorb them.
| Measure | FY2025 | FY2026 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| People enrolled | 88 | 121 | +38% |
| Completed transitional work phase | 61 | 90 | +48% |
| Placed in permanent jobs | 47 | 69 | +47% |
| Average starting wage at placement | $17.10 | $18.25 | +$1.15 |
| Paid crew hours worked by participants | 14,200 | 19,850 | +40% |
| State IDs or licenses obtained | 52 | 83 | +60% |

P16.text: Placements went to 23 employers in FY2026, up from 15 the year before. The largest were Brannock Precast, the Carver Falls Public Works Department and three regional warehouse operators. Seven of the 69 placements were in jobs with an apprenticeship track.

P17.text:
Of the people we placed in permanent jobs during FY2026, 71 percent were still employed six months after placement. In FY2025 the same figure was 58 percent.
We want to be careful with that number. Only 52 of the 69 FY2026 placements had reached the six-month mark by the time this report was written; the other 17 were placed in the spring and are not yet counted. Of the 52, we confirmed employment for 37. We lost contact with 6 people, and we count all 6 as not employed, which may understate the real rate. We also cannot say how much of the improvement comes from our work and how much comes from a tighter local labor market, since Tamsen County unemployment fell from 5.1 to 4.4 percent over the same period. We do not have a comparison group, and we are not going to pretend we do.
P17.locator: “The result we are proudest of, and its limits”

P18.text: What we can say is that the people who stayed employed were far more likely to have had at least three check-ins with a job coach in their first sixty days on the job. That pattern drives our plan for next year.
P18.locator: “The result we are proudest of, and its limits”

P19.text:
Darnell, who finished the crew phase in October and now works the night shift at Brannock Precast, told our staff:
"The crew paid me the first week. That's the part nobody else did. I didn't have to choose between rent and showing up."

P20.text:
Total FY2026 expenses were $612,400.
| Category | Amount | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Program staff (coaches, crew leads, intake) | $398,000 | 65% |
| Participant supports (transit passes, boots and gear, ID and license fees) | $96,500 | 16% |
| Housing bridge payments (first month or deposit, capped at $900) | $54,000 | 9% |
| Administration and audit | $41,900 | 7% |
| Facilities and vehicles | $22,000 | 4% |
| **Total** | **$612,400** | |
Participant crew wages are paid through the work contracts themselves and are reported separately; they are not included in the figures above. The cost per person enrolled was about $5,060, and the cost per permanent placement was about $8,875.

P21.text:
Total FY2026 revenue was $615,400, leaving a small operating surplus of $3,000.
| Source | Amount | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Tamsen County Reentry Services contract | $240,000 | 39% |
| Halvorsen Family Foundation | $150,000 | 24% |
| Carver Falls Community Trust | $95,000 | 15% |
| Individual donors (312 gifts) | $78,400 | 13% |
| Earned revenue from crew service contracts (net of wages) | $52,000 | 8% |
| **Total** | **$615,400** | |
The county contract is our largest single source and it is renewed annually. The board has set a goal of keeping it below 40 percent of revenue, and we are just under that line.

P22.text:
Three lessons shaped our planning.
First, the job is not the finish line. The first sixty days after placement are where people lose work, usually over transportation, a scheduling conflict with supervision appointments or a first conflict with a supervisor. Our coaches were stretched across intake, the crew phase and follow-up, and follow-up was what slipped.
Second, a single crew limits who we can take. With one crew of twelve, people referred in busy months waited up to three weeks to start, and we know from our own intake records that people who wait longer are less likely to show up at all.
Third, employers want to keep hiring from us. Four employers asked for more referrals than we could send this year.

P23.text:
In FY2027 we will add a second transitional work crew and a dedicated retention coach whose only job is supporting people in their first six months of permanent work.
| FY2027 expansion item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Second crew lead (full-time) and crew supervisor stipend | $72,000 |
| Retention coach (full-time, including benefits) | $64,000 |
| Second crew vehicle lease and equipment | $28,000 |
| Added participant supports for the larger cohort | $22,000 |
| **Total new cost** | **$186,000** |
With both pieces in place, we expect to enroll 160 people in FY2027, place 90 in permanent jobs and raise six-month retention to 75 percent, measured the same way we measured it this year, with lost contacts counted as not employed.

P24.text: The full FY2027 budget, including the expansion, is $798,400. We have commitments or strong renewal signals for $612,400 of it from existing sources. The remaining $186,000 is the expansion itself, which we are raising from new and existing funders this winter.

P25.text:
To the employers who took a chance, the funders who trusted a small shop with real money, and the 121 people who walked in this year and went to work: thank you.
Marisol Okafor-Reyes, Executive Director
Ridgeline Return Works, Carver Falls
